# STEP Series: full text

The specification of the OSC commands, the messages sent by the board and the configuration items of the STEP400 / STEP800 firmware v2.2.0, followed by the full text of the functional guides. It is generated from spec/osc-commands.yaml and from the English pages of the documentation, which is at https://example.invalid/step-series/. llms.txt is the table of contents of the site.

## OSC commands

### System settings

#### /setDestIp

Group: System settings. Signature: `/setDestIp`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments: none.

Description:

Sets the destination IP address (`destIp`) to where the device should send messages to, when it replies to a query or report internal state changes, etc.
The board sets the `destIp` to the sender of this message.

Until the board receives `/setDestIp`, it sends nothing to the destination (except the broadcast `/booted`), so send this command first. When `network.canSendMsgBeforeDestIp` is enabled in the configuration, it sends to `network.destIp` from the start.

To resolve the MAC address, the board sends one byte of UDP to port 9 (discard) of the broadcast address and one byte to port 9 (discard) of the destination; a Mac answers with ICMP port unreachable, which has no effect on the board. To check that the board is alive, use a command with a reply such as `/getVersion`, not `/setDestIp`.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/destIp (int)destIp[0] (int)destIp[1] (int)destIp[2] (int)destIp[3] (int)isNewDestIp`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: When this `/setDestIp` starts the resolution of the MAC address of the destination, the reply `/destIp` is sent once it has been resolved, so it can come later than before (a few ms on a wired network, up to a few seconds on Wi-Fi). If it does not come, send `/setDestIp` again. A `/setDestIp` that starts no resolution (for example one sent every second as a heartbeat) is answered at once.
- v2.2.0: Messages to the destination (replies, reports, errors) are dropped while the MAC address is being resolved (up to a few seconds). The broadcast `/booted` is still sent.
- v2.2.0: A `/setDestIp` from a different device with the same IP address (another PC or network adapter), sent 1.5 s or more after the last packet from the old one, now makes the board send to the new device. Before, the board kept sending to the old MAC address until it was restarted.
- v2.2.0: A send to a destination that has never answered ARP (for example a wrong destination address) blocks the processing for about 41 ms (1.6 s or more before). It no longer happens for every message: the sends to that destination are paused for 1 s: the messages in that time are dropped, not sent later. A packet received from that destination resumes the sends at once. The broadcast `/booted` is not affected.

#### /getVersion

Group: System settings. Signature: `/getVersion`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments: none.

Description:

Returns the firmware version burnt on the chip.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/version (string)version`

#### /getConfigName

Group: System settings. Signature: `/getConfigName`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments: none.

Description:

Returns `/configName`: the configuration name, whether the microSD card could be used, whether a configuration file was opened and parsed, and the path of the file.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/configName (string)configName (int)sdInitializeSucceeded (int)configFileOpenSucceeded (int)configFileParseSucceeded (string)configFilename`

See also: `/setConfigName`

#### /reportError

Group: System settings. Signature: `/reportError (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `enable` (bool, initial value true (Enable), configuration item `network.reportError`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Enables or disables the automatic message notification for `/error/command` and `/error/osc`.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/error/command (string)errorText (int)motorID` (notification)
- `/error/osc (string)errorText` (notification)

#### /setConfigName

Group: System settings. Signature: `/setConfigName (string)configName`. Added in v2.1.0. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `configName` (string, initial value Default (firmware) / "" (template), configuration item `information.configName`): Configuration name string

Description:

Sets the configuration name stored in the device. This is a user-editable label for identifying configurations and is distinct from the on-disk filename.

The name changes only in the board until it is saved with `/saveConfig`: `/getConfigName` returns the new name at once, but a restart before the save brings back the name in the configuration file.

See also: `/getConfigName`, `/saveConfig`

#### /saveConfig

Group: System settings. Signature: `/saveConfig`. Added in v2.1.0. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments: none.

Description:

Saves the current running configuration to the microSD card as a JSON file. The file is the one read at start-up, or `/config.txt` if no file was read. The path can be changed with `F<path>` over USB serial.

The configuration is written to a hidden temporary file `.<name>.tmp` in the same folder first, and the saved file is replaced only after that has been written. A save that fails while the temporary file is being written leaves the saved file as it was.

The card is checked only at start-up. With no usable card at start-up (a card inserted afterwards, or an exFAT card) the reply is `No SD card`; with a card removed after start-up, a full card or a missing folder it is `SD open failed`. The saved configuration is applied at the next start-up.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/saveConfig (string)message` (when: Saved)
- `/error/saveConfig (string)errorText` (when: Failed)

See also: `/configName`, `/setConfigName`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The configuration is written to a hidden temporary file `.<name>.tmp` in the same folder, and the saved file is replaced only after the temporary file has been written and closed. A save that fails (the card or the folder is full, the folder does not exist, a write error) leaves the saved file as it was and replies `SD open failed`. Before, the old file was deleted first, so a failed save left no configuration file on the card. If the power is cut after the old file is deleted and before the new one is renamed, or if the rename fails (`SD open failed`), only the temporary file remains (there is no recovery at start-up). Its name starts with `.`, so it is not read as a configuration file (see `/configName`).
- v2.2.0: Arduino IDE build: saving to an exFAT card (SDXC, 64 GB or more by default) deleted the file on the card and replied `SD open failed`. Now the Arduino IDE build is the same as the PlatformIO build: an exFAT card is not used (`No SD card`) and nothing on it is touched. Format the card as FAT16 or FAT32.

#### /resetDevice

Group: System settings. Signature: `/resetDevice`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments: none.

Description:

Resets the entire device. A programmatic version of physically pressing the RESET switch.

After the restart, `/booted` is sent with `resetCause` 5 (software reset).

Changes:

- v2.2.0: First stops the turning motors that have the electromagnetic brake enabled and not engaged with a hard stop, engages their brakes and waits for the longest `brakeTransitionDuration` of them (at most 1 s), then restarts. Motors without the brake are not stopped by the firmware. Before, the board restarted at once.
- v2.2.0: Resets with a software reset: `/booted` reports `resetCause` 5.

### Motor driver settings

#### /setMicrostepMode

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/setMicrostepMode (int)motorID (int)STEP_SEL`. Executable timing: High Z state.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `STEP_SEL` (int, range 0-7, initial value 7 (1/128 microstep), configuration item `driverSettings.stepMode`): Microstepping mode
  - `0`: Full-step
  - `1`: Half-step
  - `2`: 1/4 microstep
  - `3`: 1/8 microstep
  - `4`: 1/16 microstep
  - `5`: 1/32 microstep
  - `6`: 1/64 microstep
  - `7`: 1/128 microstep

Description:

Sets the microstepping mode.
In the constant-current control mode (current mode), only full-step to 1/16 microstep is available.

The motor must be HiZ. A motor holding its position is not HiZ: send `/softHiZ` or `/hardHiZ` first, otherwise `MotorNotHiZ` is replied and nothing is applied. On STEP400 in the current mode, a step mode finer than 1/16 replies `CommandIgnored`.

A value outside 0-7 is not rejected: it is converted to 8 bits and then limited to 0-7 (-1 becomes 7, 256 becomes 0).

Errors:

- `MotorNotHiZ`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the outputs are HiZ, and the motor is not HiZ. A motor holding its position is not HiZ: send `/softHiZ` or `/hardHiZ` first. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.
- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getMicrostepMode`, `/setCurrentMode`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The motor must be HiZ; otherwise `/error/command MotorNotHiZ` is replied and nothing is applied. Before, the driver ignored the write while the firmware variable and the saved configuration took the new value.
- v2.2.0: STEP400 in the current mode: a step mode finer than 1/16 replies `CommandIgnored` (the PowerSTEP01 current mode goes up to 1/16).

#### /getMicrostepMode

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getMicrostepMode (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the mode of microstepping. See `/setMicrostepMode` for STEP_SEL.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/microstepMode (int)motorID (int)STEP_SEL`

#### /enableLowSpeedOptimize

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/enableLowSpeedOptimize (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value false (Disable), configuration item `voltageMode.lowSpeedOptimizeEnable`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Enable/disable low speed optimization feature which compensate phase current distortion at a very low speed using a small driving voltage. When this optimization is enabled, speed profile minimum speed (`Min speed`) is force to zero. Only work with voltage mode. See data sheets for details.

Errors:

- `MotorNotStopped`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the motor is stopped or HiZ, and the motor is turning. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/setLowSpeedOptimizeThreshold`, `/setMinSpeed`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `/error/command MotorNotStopped` and nothing is applied.

#### /setLowSpeedOptimizeThreshold

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/setLowSpeedOptimizeThreshold (int)motorID (float)lowSpeedOptimizationThreshold`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `lowSpeedOptimizationThreshold` (float, range 0-976.3 step/s, initial value 20, configuration item `voltageMode.lowSpeedOptimize`): Low speed optimization threshold

Description:

Set the threshold for phase current distortion compensation at very low speed. For details, refer to "Low speed optimization" section in the corresponding datasheet.

No reply is sent. Read the value back with `/getLowSpeedOptimizeThreshold`.

While the low speed optimization is enabled, the motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `MotorNotStopped` and nothing is applied.

Errors:

- `MotorNotStopped`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the motor is stopped or HiZ, and the motor is turning. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/getLowSpeedOptimizeThreshold`, `/enableLowSpeedOptimize`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: While the low speed optimization is enabled, a turning motor replies `/error/command MotorNotStopped` and nothing is applied.

#### /getLowSpeedOptimizeThreshold

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getLowSpeedOptimizeThreshold (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the current value of the low speed optimization threshold.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/lowSpeedOptimizeThreshold (int)motorID (float)lowSpeedOptimizeThreshold (int)optimizationEnabled`

#### /enableBusyReport

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/enableBusyReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value false (Disable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportBUSY`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Automatically sends out notification if the BUSY status of the specified motor has changed. The notification message is same as the response from `/getBusy` command.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/busy (int)motorID (int)state` (notification)

#### /getBusy

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getBusy (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns the BUSY state of the specified motor.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/busy (int)motorID (int)state`

#### /enableHizReport

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/enableHizReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value false (Disable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportHiZ`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Following message is sent automatically when there is a change in the High Z (high impedance) state of the specified motor.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/HiZ (int)motorID (int)state` (notification)

#### /getHiZ

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getHiZ (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Requests the High Z (high impedance) state of the specified motor.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/HiZ (int)motorID (int)state`

#### /enableDirReport

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/enableDirReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value false (Disable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportDir`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Following message is sent automatically when there is a change in the direction of the specified motor.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/dir (int)motorID (int)direction` (notification)

#### /getDir

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getDir (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Requests the direction of the specified motor.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

#### /enableMotorStatusReport

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/enableMotorStatusReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value false (Disable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportMotorStatus`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Following message will be sent automatically when there is conditional change in the operating status (MOT_STATUS) of the specified motor. The response message is same as the reply from the `/getMotorStatus` command.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/motorStatus (int)motorID (int)MOT_STATUS` (notification)

#### /getMotorStatus

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getMotorStatus (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the operating status (MOT_STATUS) of the specified motor.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/motorStatus (int)motorID (int)MOT_STATUS`

#### /setPositionReportInterval

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/setPositionReportInterval (int)motorID (int)interval`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `interval` (int, range 0-65535 ms, initial value 0, configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportPositionInterval`): transmit interval

Description:

Send the current position (`ABS_POS`) of the specified motor with the specified interval. Disabled with the interval 0.

When this function enabled, `/setPositionListReportInterval` will be automatically disabled and stop the transmitting.

An interval above 65535 replies `CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. A negative interval disables the report, as 0.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/position (int)motorID (int)ABS_POS` (notification)

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getPosition`, `/setPositionListReportInterval`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A value above 65535 replies `/error/command CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. Before, 32768 and above were read as negative and disabled the report. A negative interval still disables it.
- v2.2.0: When the report is enabled (interval above 0) for one motor, the saved position list report interval is cleared too, as it was for 255. Before, a configuration saved after switching from the list report to one motor's report started the list report again at the next start and cleared the motor's report.

#### /setPositionListReportInterval

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/setPositionListReportInterval (int)interval`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `interval` (int, range 0-65535 ms, initial value 0, configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportPositionListInterval`): transmit interval

Description:

Send a single message with a list of the current position (`ABS_POS`) of all motors with the specified interval. Disabled with the interval 0.

When this function enabled, `/setPositionReportInterval` will be disabled automatically for all motors and stop the transmitting.

An interval above 65535 replies `CommandIgnored` with the motor ID 255 and nothing is applied. A negative interval disables the report, as 0.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/positionList (int)position1 ... (int)positionN` (notification)

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getPositionList`, `/setPositionReportInterval`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A value above 65535 replies `/error/command CommandIgnored 255` and nothing is applied. Before, 32768 and above were read as negative and disabled the report. A negative interval still disables it.

#### /getAdcVal

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getAdcVal (int)motorID`. Available on STEP400 only. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Acquires ADC_OUT register values from the PowerSTEP01 chip. This register stores 5-bit AD-converted voltage reading from ADC pin. This pin is pull-upped with 10kOhm resistor and wired to LIMITSW connector.

STEP400 only. The firmware also accepts the command on STEP800, but it is not meaningful there.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/adcVal (int)motorID (int)ADC_OUT`

#### /getStatus

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getStatus (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the STATUS of the motor driver (PowerSTEP01 for STEP400/L6470 for STEP800). The STATUS includes the status of the motor, alarms and switches.

Refer to "STATUS" in the data sheet for the information contained in the registers. Some of bits are latched and reset when STATUS registers are read out. Because the device firmware constantly obtains the STATUS values, these values are immediately reset. It is possible to set up these events to be reported separately, so please use those commands.

This command does not clear the latched flags; only the status poll of the firmware (every 5 ms) does.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/status (int)motorID (int)status`

See also: `/getStatusList`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Reads the STATUS register with GetParam instead of GetStatus, so it no longer clears the latched driver flags (e.g. OCD, stall flags, UVLO, SW_EVN). The register values are the same. Only the status poll of the firmware (every 5 ms) clears them now, so a `/getStatus` sent right after another can show a flag the earlier reply showed (until the next poll, up to 5 ms).

#### /getConfigRegister

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getConfigRegister (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Acquires the CONFIG register value from the motor driver (PowerSTEP01 or L6470). The information stored in CONFIG register includes motor, alarm and switch status.

The CONFIG register stores various settings for the motor driver. Please refer the datasheet of the PowerSTEP01/L6470 for detail.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/configRegister (int)motorID (int)CONFIG`

#### /resetMotorDriver

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/resetMotorDriver (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Resets the motor driver (PowerSTEP01/L6470) and rewrites the setting.

With the electromagnetic brake enabled, the command is accepted only while the brake is engaged or after `/free` (the motor is HiZ); otherwise it replies `CommandIgnored`. When it is accepted (also with the brake disabled), it cancels pending motion and the servo mode. A command that is refused (`CommandIgnored`) cancels nothing.

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

Changes:

- v2.2.0: With the electromagnetic brake enabled, accepted only while the brake is engaged or after `/free`; otherwise `/error/command CommandIgnored`. Before, it made the driver HiZ with the brake released.
- v2.2.0: Cancels pending motion (a `/goTo` etc. waiting for the BUSY flag, the homing, the servo mode) when it is accepted, also with the brake disabled. A refused command (`CommandIgnored`) cancels nothing.
- v2.2.0: The settings applied again after the reset include those made with the Raw commands (see `/setAccRaw`).

#### /getStatusList

Group: Motor driver settings. Signature: `/getStatusList`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments: none.

Description:

Gets the STATUS registers of all motors at once. See `/getStatus` for the contents of the register.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/statusList (int)status1 ... (int)statusN`

See also: `/getStatus`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Reads the STATUS registers with GetParam instead of GetStatus, so it no longer clears the latched driver flags. See `/getStatus`.

### Alarm settings

#### /enableUvloReport

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/enableUvloReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value true (Enable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportUVLO`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Set the notification message when UVLO (Undervoltage Lockout) occurs in the specified motor driver.
UVLO occurs when the supplied voltage to the motor driver falls below the UVLO turn-off threshold voltage, with or without notification. In this state, the motor cannot be operated. It will be reset when the supply voltage is above the UVLO turn-on threshold.

These thresholds are different between STEP400(PowerSTEP01) and STEP800(L6470). For details, please refer to the corresponding datasheets.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/uvlo (int)motorID (int)state` (notification)

See also: `/getUvlo`

#### /getUvlo

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/getUvlo (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the current state of UVLO

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/uvlo (int)motorID (int)state`

#### /enableThermalStatusReport

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/enableThermalStatusReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value true (Enable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportThermalStatus`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Sends a notification message when a change in the temperature status (thermalStatus) of the specified motor driver is detected. On bridge shutdown or device shutdown, the motor state will automatically enter High Z state with or without notification.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/thermalStatus (int)motorID (int)thermalStatus` (notification)

See also: `/getThermalStatus`

#### /getThermalStatus

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/getThermalStatus (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the current condition of the ThermalStatus. Thermal status thresholds are different between STEP400(PowerSTEP01) and STEP800(L6470).

In the bridge shutdown and device shutdown states, the motor goes into the High Z state with or without notification.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/thermalStatus (int)motorID (int)thermalStatus`

#### /enableOverCurrentReport

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/enableOverCurrentReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value true (Enable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportOCD`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Set to send a notification when the specified motor driver goes into an overcurrent state (OCD, Over Current Detection).
When overcurrent is detected, the device automatically enters High Z state regardless of whether a notification being sent. The threshold can be set with `/setOverCurrentThreshold`.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/overCurrent (int)motorID` (notification)

#### /setOverCurrentThreshold

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/setOverCurrentThreshold (int)motorID (int)OCD_TH`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `OCD_TH` (int, range 0-31 (STEP400), 0-15 (STEP800), initial value STEP400: 15 (5A); STEP800: 7 (3A), configuration item `alarmAndReport.OCThreshold`): Overcurrent detection threshold

Description:

Sets the overcurrent threshold. The setting value range and corresponding currents are different between STEP400(PowerSTEP01) and STEP800(L6470).

A value above the range is not rejected; it wraps around: the value after the maximum is 0 (on STEP800, 16 becomes 0 and 17 becomes 1).

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/overCurrentThreshold (int)motorID (float)overCurrentThreshold`

See also: `/getOverCurrentThreshold`, `/enableOverCurrentReport`

#### /getOverCurrentThreshold

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/getOverCurrentThreshold (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Get the threshold of overcurrent.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/overCurrentThreshold (int)motorID (float)overCurrentThreshold`

#### /enableStallReport

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/enableStallReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value false (Disable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportStall`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

The threshold can be set by `/setStallThreshold`.
When the stall is detected by the specified motor driver, the following message is sent automatically.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/stall (int)motorID` (notification)

#### /setStallThreshold

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/setStallThreshold (int)motorID (int)STALL_TH`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `STALL_TH` (int, range 0-31 (STEP400), 0-127 (STEP800), initial value STEP400: 31 (10A); STEP800: 127 (4A), configuration item `voltageMode.STALL_TH`): Stall detection threshold

Description:

Sets the threshold for stall detection. The setting value range and corresponding currents are different between STEP400(PowerSTEP01) and STEP800(L6470).

Stall detection lets the driver detect, from the motor current, that the motor can no longer turn against the load. Find a threshold (`/setStallThreshold`) as close as possible to, and slightly above, the current actually flowing. A small loss of steps cannot be detected, but a large position error may be.

A value above the range is not rejected; it wraps around: the value after the maximum is 0 (on STEP800, 128 becomes 0 and 129 becomes 1).

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/stallThreshold (int)motorID (float)stallThreshold`

See also: `/getStallThreshold`, `/enableStallReport`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Also changes the saved STALL_TH (`/saveConfig`, `/resetMotorDriver`). Before, it changed the register only.

#### /getStallThreshold

Group: Alarm settings. Signature: `/getStallThreshold (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the stall detection threshold.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/stallThreshold (int)motorID (float)stallThreshold`

  - `1`: Prohibit
  - `0`: Allow

See also: `/getProhibitMotionOnHomeSw`, `/setHomingDirection`

Changes:

### Voltage and current mode settings

#### /setVoltageMode

Group: Voltage and current mode settings. Signature: `/setVoltageMode (int)motorID`. Available on STEP400 only. Executable timing: High Z state.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Switches the specified motor to the voltage drive mode.

Note: This command is only available in STEP400.
STEP800 is always in this voltage mode and cannot change.

Errors:

- `MotorNotHiZ`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the outputs are HiZ, and the motor is not HiZ. A motor holding its position is not HiZ: send `/softHiZ` or `/hardHiZ` first. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.
- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/setCurrentMode`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The outputs must be HiZ; otherwise `/error/command MotorNotHiZ` is replied and nothing is applied.
- v2.2.0: The mode is changed only if the driver took it (STEP_MODE is read back); otherwise `/error/command CommandIgnored`. Before, the stored mode was changed while the driver kept the old one, so `/setKval` and `/setTval` then wrote the wrong registers.

#### /setKval

Group: Voltage and current mode settings. Signature: `/setKval (int)motorID (int)holdKVAL (int)runKVAL (int)accKVAL (int)decKVAL`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `holdKVAL` (int, range 0-255, initial value 0, configuration item `voltageMode.KVAL_HOLD`): KVAL when stopped
- `runKVAL` (int, range 0-255, initial value 16, configuration item `voltageMode.KVAL_RUN`): KVAL in constant speed operation
- `accKVAL` (int, range 0-255, initial value 16, configuration item `voltageMode.KVAL_ACC`): KVAL during acceleration
- `decKVAL` (int, range 0-255, initial value 16, configuration item `voltageMode.KVAL_DEC`): KVAL during deceleration

Description:

Sets the four KVALs together.

A value outside 0-255 is not rejected: it is limited to 0-255.

On STEP400 in the current mode only the stored setting changes; `/setVoltageMode` writes it to the registers.

See also: `/getKval`, `/setHoldKval`, `/setRunKval`, `/setAccKval`, `/setDecKval`

#### /getKval

Group: Voltage and current mode settings. Signature: `/getKval (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Get the four KVALs together.

With the electromagnetic brake enabled and the voltage mode, KVAL_HOLD is raised to at least half of KVAL_RUN whenever the motor is energized again (from engaged, engaging or after `/free`), and this command returns the raised value. In the current mode TVAL_HOLD is raised instead.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/kval (int)motorID (int)holdKVAL (int)runKVAL (int)accKVAL (int)decKVAL`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Returns the settings (what `/setKval` sets and `/saveConfig` saves) instead of the driver registers. In the current mode the KVAL registers keep the value from before; in the voltage mode they are the registers. KVAL_HOLD raised for a motor with the electromagnetic brake is returned too. STEP800: the reply is the same as before.

#### /setBemfParam

Group: Voltage and current mode settings. Signature: `/setBemfParam (int)motorID (int)INT_SPEED (int)ST_SLP (int)FN_SLP_ACC (int)FN_SLP_DEC`. Executable timing: High Z state.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `INT_SPEED` (int, range 0-16383, initial value 1032, configuration item `voltageMode.INT_SPEED`): INT_SPEED register value
- `ST_SLP` (int, range 0-255, initial value 25, configuration item `voltageMode.ST_SLP`): ST_SLP register value
- `FN_SLP_ACC` (int, range 0-255, initial value 41, configuration item `voltageMode.FN_SLP_ACC`): FN_SLP_ACC register value
- `FN_SLP_DEC` (int, range 0-255, initial value 41, configuration item `voltageMode.FN_SLP_DEC`): FN_SLP_DEC register value

Description:

Sets BEMF compensation parameter register. For the values for each parameter, refer voltage mode and current mode.

The outputs must be HiZ; otherwise `MotorNotHiZ` is replied and nothing is applied.

A value outside the range is not rejected: INT_SPEED is limited to 0-16383 and the other parameters to 0-255.

Errors:

- `MotorNotHiZ`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the outputs are HiZ, and the motor is not HiZ. A motor holding its position is not HiZ: send `/softHiZ` or `/hardHiZ` first. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/getBemfParam`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The outputs must be HiZ (INT_SPEED, ST_SLP, FN_SLP_ACC and FN_SLP_DEC are writable only in HiZ); otherwise `/error/command MotorNotHiZ` and nothing is applied.

#### /setCurrentMode

Group: Voltage and current mode settings. Signature: `/setCurrentMode (int)motorID`. Available on STEP400 only. Executable timing: High Z state.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Switches the specified motor to the current drive mode.

The PowerSTEP01 current mode goes up to 1/16 microsteps: a finer microstep mode is lowered to 1/16, and the stored setting (`/setMicrostepMode`, `driverSettings.stepMode`) is changed with it.

Errors:

- `MotorNotHiZ`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the outputs are HiZ, and the motor is not HiZ. A motor holding its position is not HiZ: send `/softHiZ` or `/hardHiZ` first. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.
- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/setVoltageMode`, `/setMicrostepMode`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The outputs must be HiZ; otherwise `/error/command MotorNotHiZ` is replied and nothing is applied.
- v2.2.0: The mode is changed only if the driver took it (STEP_MODE is read back); otherwise `/error/command CommandIgnored`. Before, the stored mode was changed while the driver kept the old one, so `/setKval` and `/setTval` then wrote the wrong registers.

#### /setTval

Group: Voltage and current mode settings. Signature: `/setTval (int)motorID (int)holdTVAL (int)runTVAL (int)accTVAL (int)decTVAL`. Available on STEP400 only. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `holdTVAL` (int, range 0-64, initial value 0 (78.125mA), configuration item `currentMode.TVAL_HOLD`): TVAL when stopped
- `runTVAL` (int, range 0-64, initial value 16 (1.328A), configuration item `currentMode.TVAL_RUN`): TVAL in constant speed operation
- `accTVAL` (int, range 0-64, initial value 16 (1.328A), configuration item `currentMode.TVAL_ACC`): TVAL during acceleration
- `decTVAL` (int, range 0-64, initial value 16 (1.328A), configuration item `currentMode.TVAL_DEC`): TVAL during deceleration

Description:

Sets the four TVALs together.
In STEP400, the TVAL is as follows.

A value outside 0-64 is not rejected: it is limited to 0-64. The upper limit 64 (about 5 A) is a safety limit of the firmware.

In the voltage mode only the stored setting changes; `/setCurrentMode` writes it to the registers.

See also: `/getTval`, `/getTval_mA`, `/setHoldTval`, `/setRunTval`, `/setAccTval`, `/setDecTval`

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Get the four TVAL types together.

With the electromagnetic brake enabled and the current mode, TVAL_HOLD is raised to at least half of TVAL_RUN whenever the motor is energized again (from engaged, engaging or after `/free`), and this command returns the raised value. In the voltage mode KVAL_HOLD is raised instead.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/tval (int)motorID (int)holdTVAL (int)runTVAL (int)accTVAL (int)decTVAL`

See also: `/getTval_mA`

- v2.2.0: Returns the settings (what `/setTval` sets and `/saveConfig` saves) instead of the driver registers. In the voltage mode the TVAL registers keep the value from before. TVAL_HOLD raised for a motor with the electromagnetic brake is returned too.

#### /setDecayModeParam

Group: Voltage and current mode settings. Signature: `/setDecayModeParam (int)motorID (int)T_FAST (int)TON_MIN (int)TOFF_MIN`. Available on STEP400 only. Executable timing: High Z state.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `T_FAST` (int, range 0-255, initial value 25, configuration item `currentMode.T_FAST`): T_FAST register value
- `TON_MIN` (int, range 0-127, initial value 41, configuration item `currentMode.TON_MIN`): TON_MIN register value
- `TOFF_MIN` (int, range 0-127, initial value 41, configuration item `currentMode.TOFF_MIN`): TOFF_MIN register value

Description:

Sets registers for the current control algorithm parameters. For the each register values, refer the datasheet of the PowerSTEP01.

The outputs must be HiZ; otherwise `MotorNotHiZ` is replied and nothing is applied.

TON_MIN and TOFF_MIN are 7 bit (0-127): a value outside it replies `CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. A T_FAST outside 0-255 is limited to 0-255.

Errors:

- `MotorNotHiZ`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the outputs are HiZ, and the motor is not HiZ. A motor holding its position is not HiZ: send `/softHiZ` or `/hardHiZ` first. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.
- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getDecayModeParam`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: TON_MIN and TOFF_MIN are 0-127 (7 bit); a value outside it replies `/error/command CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. Before, 128-255 were taken modulo 128 by the driver while the saved value stayed 128-255. T_FAST is 0-255 as before.
- v2.2.0: The outputs must be HiZ; otherwise `/error/command MotorNotHiZ` and nothing is applied.

### Speed profile

#### /setSpeedProfile

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/setSpeedProfile (int)motorID (float)acc (float)dec (float)maxSpeed`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `acc` (float, range 14.55-59575 step/s/s, initial value 1000 (firmware) / 2000 (template), configuration item `speedProfile.acc`): acceleration
- `dec` (float, range 14.55-59590 (STEP400), 14.55-59575 (STEP800) step/s/s, initial value 1000 (firmware) / 2000 (template), configuration item `speedProfile.dec`): deceleration
- `maxSpeed` (float, range 15.25-15610 step/s, initial value 650 (firmware) / 620 (template), configuration item `speedProfile.maxSpeed`): maximum speed

Description:

Sets the acc, dec, and maxSpeed of the speed profile together.

The speed profile is the set of acceleration, deceleration and maximum speed held in the motor driver. It is not sent with each command: it applies to every motion after it is written (`/run`, `/goTo` and so on). The minimum speed is set separately with `/setMinSpeed`.

ACC and DEC are rounded to the nearest register value, so the written value can differ by 1 LSB. MAX_SPEED alone is writable at any time, but nothing is written to a motor that replies with `MotorNotStopped`. A value outside the range is limited by the driver library. On STEP400, a maximum speed of 0 is written as 1 (the register value 0 is reserved).

Errors:

- `MotorNotStopped`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the motor is stopped or HiZ, and the motor is turning. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/getSpeedProfile`, `/setAcc`, `/setDec`, `/setMaxSpeed`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `/error/command MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old values.
- v2.2.0: `acc` and `dec` are rounded to the nearest register value, so the written value can differ by 1 LSB.
- v2.2.0: STEP400: a maximum speed of 0 is written as 1 (the register value 0 is reserved).

#### /getSpeedProfile

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/getSpeedProfile (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the acc, dec, and maxSpeed of the speed profile together.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/speedProfile (int)motorID (float)acc (float)dec (float)maxSpeed`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The acceleration and deceleration are reported about 4.9% smaller than before; they now match the datasheet (driver libraries v1.2.0).

#### /setFullstepSpeed

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/setFullstepSpeed (int)motorID (float)fullstepSpeed`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `fullstepSpeed` (float, range 7.63-15625 step/s, initial value 15610 (firmware) / 15625 (template), configuration item `speedProfile.fullStepSpeed`): threshold

Description:

Sets the threshold at which the microstepping mode automatically switches to full-step mode.

A value above the range is limited to 15625 step/s by the driver library. A value from 0 up to the lower end of the range is written as the lower end (7.63 step/s). A negative value below about -7.6 is not limited to the lower end: the driver library converts it to a huge unsigned number and limits that to the maximum, so it becomes 15625 step/s.

See also: `/getFullstepSpeed`

#### /getFullstepSpeed

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/getFullstepSpeed (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the threshold at which the microstepping mode automatically switches to full-step mode.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/fullstepSpeed (int)motorID (float)fullstepSpeed`

#### /setMaxSpeed

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/setMaxSpeed (int)motorID (float)maxSpeed`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `maxSpeed` (float, range 15.25-15610 step/s, initial value 650 (firmware) / 620 (template), configuration item `speedProfile.maxSpeed`): maximum speed

Description:

Set the maximum speed of the speed profile

A value outside the range is limited by the driver library. On STEP400, a maximum speed of 0 is written as 1 (the register value 0 is reserved).

See also: `/setSpeedProfile`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: STEP400: a maximum speed of 0 is written as 1 (the register value 0 is reserved). STEP800 is unchanged.

#### /setAcc

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/setAcc (int)motorID (float)acc`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `acc` (float, range 14.55-59575 step/s/s, initial value 1000 (firmware) / 2000 (template), configuration item `speedProfile.acc`): acceleration

Description:

Sets the acceleration of the speed profile.

The value is rounded to the nearest register value, so the written value can differ by 1 LSB. A value outside the range is limited by the driver library.

The motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value.

Errors:

- `MotorNotStopped`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the motor is stopped or HiZ, and the motor is turning. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/setSpeedProfile`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `/error/command MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value.
- v2.2.0: Rounds to the nearest register value, so the written value can differ by 1 LSB.

#### /setDec

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `dec` (float, range 14.55-59590 (STEP400), 14.55-59575 (STEP800) step/s/s, initial value 1000 (firmware) / 2000 (template), configuration item `speedProfile.dec`): deceleration

Description:

Sets the deceleration of the speed profile.

The value is rounded to the nearest register value, so the written value can differ by 1 LSB. A value outside the range is limited by the driver library.

The motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value.

- `MotorNotStopped`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the motor is stopped or HiZ, and the motor is turning. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/setSpeedProfile`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `/error/command MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value.

#### /setMinSpeed

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/setMinSpeed (int)motorID (float)minSpeed`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `minSpeed` (float, range 0-976.3 step/s, initial value 0, configuration item `speedProfile.minSpeed`): Minimum speed

Description:

Set the speed profile minimum speed. This value is also used for the motor speed of `/releaseSw`. When Low speed optimization (`/enableLowSpeedOptimize`) is enabled, the minimum speed of the speed profile is set to zero.

While the low speed optimization is disabled, the motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value. While it is enabled, only the saved value changes and no error is sent.

A value above the range is limited to 976.3 step/s by the driver library. A negative value below about -0.24 is not limited to 0: the driver library converts it to a huge unsigned number and limits that to the maximum, so it becomes 976.3 step/s.

Errors:

- `MotorNotStopped`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the motor is stopped or HiZ, and the motor is turning. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/getMinSpeed`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: While the low speed optimization is disabled, the motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `/error/command MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value.
- v2.2.0: `/setMinSpeed 255` (all motors) checks the low speed optimization setting of each motor. It read an invalid array element.

#### /getMinSpeed

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/getMinSpeed (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Return the speed profile minimum speed.

Returns 0.0 for a motor with the low speed optimization enabled: the MIN_SPEED register then holds the optimization threshold (read it with `/getLowSpeedOptimizeThreshold`) and the actual minimum speed is 0. For a motor with the optimization disabled, it returns the MIN_SPEED register value of the driver in step/s.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/minSpeed (int)motorID (float)minSpeed`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Returns 0.0 for a motor with the low speed optimization enabled. A single motor returned the MIN_SPEED register value (the threshold) and `255` (all motors) returned the stored minimum speed setting; both behave the same now.

#### /getSpeed

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/getSpeed (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns the current motor speed.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/speed (int)motorID (float)speed`

#### /setSpeedProfileRaw

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/setSpeedProfileRaw (int)motorID (int)acc (int)dec (int)maxSpeed`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `acc` (int, range 0-4095): acceleration (raw register value)
- `dec` (int, range 0-4095): deceleration (raw register value)
- `maxSpeed` (int, range 0-1023): maximum speed (raw register value)

Description:

Sets the acc, dec, and maxSpeed of the speed profile using raw driver IC register values.

A value outside the range is not rejected: it is converted to 16 bits (70000 becomes 4464) and then masked to the width of the register by the driver. The motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value.

Errors:

- `MotorNotStopped`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the motor is stopped or HiZ, and the motor is turning. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/getSpeedProfileRaw`, `/setSpeedProfile`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Also sets the acceleration, deceleration and maximum speed setting that `/saveConfig` saves and `/resetMotorDriver` applies again. Before, only the register was changed, so a reset or a saved configuration brought back the value from before.
- v2.2.0: The motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `/error/command MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value.

#### /getSpeedProfileRaw

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/getSpeedProfileRaw (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the acc, dec, and maxSpeed of the speed profile as raw driver IC register values.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/speedProfileRaw (int)motorID (int)acc (int)dec (int)maxSpeed`

#### /setMaxSpeedRaw

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/setMaxSpeedRaw (int)motorID (int)maxSpeed`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `maxSpeed` (int, range 0-1023): maximum speed (raw register value)

Description:

Sets the maximum speed of the speed profile using a raw register value.

A value outside the range is not rejected: it is converted to 16 bits (70000 becomes 4464) and then masked to the width of the register by the driver.

`/setMaxSpeedRaw 0` writes 0, also on STEP400.

See also: `/setMaxSpeed`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Also sets the maximum speed setting that `/saveConfig` saves and `/resetMotorDriver` applies again. Before, only the register was changed, so a reset or a saved configuration brought back the value from before.

#### /setMinSpeedRaw

Group: Speed profile. Signature: `/setMinSpeedRaw (int)motorID (int)minSpeed`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `minSpeed` (int, range 0-4095): minimum speed (raw register value)

Description:

Sets the minimum speed of the speed profile using a raw register value.

A value outside the range is not rejected: it is converted to 16 bits (70000 becomes 4464) and then masked to the width of the register by the driver. While the low speed optimization is disabled, the motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value. While it is enabled, only the saved value changes and no error is sent.

Errors:

- `MotorNotStopped`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the motor is stopped or HiZ, and the motor is turning. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/setMinSpeed`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Also sets the minimum speed setting that `/saveConfig` saves and `/resetMotorDriver` applies again. Before, only the register was changed, so a reset or a saved configuration brought back the value from before.
- v2.2.0: While the low speed optimization is disabled, the motor must be stopped or HiZ; a turning motor replies `/error/command MotorNotStopped` and keeps its old value.
- v2.2.0: Bit 12 is ignored (it switched the low speed optimization on without `/enableLowSpeedOptimize`). While the optimization is on, the command only changes the saved value, as `/setMinSpeed` does.

#### /setFullstepSpeedRaw

Arguments:

- `fullstepSpeed` (int, range 0-1023): full-step speed threshold (raw register value)

### Homing

#### /homing

Group: Homing. Signature: `/homing (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Start the homing movement. Move towards origin direction, stop when the HOME switch is activated. Then the motor reverses the direction and move slowly, halts when the HOME switch is not active anymore, then reset location to zero at the current point.

This is equivalent to the following actions of executing `/goUntil` command, and after the motor stops on HOME switch activation, execute `/releaseSw` command.

The `homingDirection` and the `homingSpeed` can be set by `/setHomingDirection` and `/setHomingSpeed` commands, as well as configuring from the browser configuration tool.

Time-out can be set for each of the `/goUntil` and `/releaseSw` commands. The controller halts the motor movement if the sensor state has not changed during this time frame. The time-out values can be set from `/setGoUntilTimeout` and from the `/setReleaseSwTimeout` command.

Depending on the state change on the homing movement, following response will be sent.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (notification)

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).
- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `GoUntilTimeout`: Timeout while executing `/goUntil` command.
- `ReleaseSwTimeout`: Timeout while executing `/releaseSw` command.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/getHomingStatus`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: While the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`), replies `/error/command BrakeEngaged` and does nothing. Before, it set the homing state although it did not start.

#### /getHomingStatus

Group: Homing. Signature: `/getHomingStatus (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns current state of homing movement.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus`

#### /setHomingDirection

Group: Homing. Signature: `/setHomingDirection (int)motorID (bool)direction`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `direction` (bool, initial value 0 (Reverse), configuration item `driverSettings.homingDirection`)
  - `1`: Forward
  - `0`: Reverse

Description:

Sets the `homingDirection` for the `/homing` command. It can be also configured from the browser configuration tool.

See also: `/getHomingDirection`

#### /getHomingDirection

Group: Homing. Signature: `/getHomingDirection (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

#### /setHomingSpeed

Group: Homing. Signature: `/setHomingSpeed (int)motorID (float)speed`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `speed` (float, range 0-15610 step/s, initial value 50, configuration item `driverSettings.homingSpeed`): homing speed

Description:

Sets the `homingSpeed` when executing the command `/homing`. It can be configured from the browser configuration tool.

A value outside the range is not rejected: it is limited to 0-15610.

See also: `/getHomingSpeed`

#### /getHomingSpeed

Group: Homing. Signature: `/getHomingSpeed (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns `homingSpeed` parameter.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingSpeed (int)motorID (float)homingSpeed`

#### /goUntil

Group: Homing. Signature: `/goUntil (int)motorID (bool)ACT (float)speed`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `ACT` (bool)
  - `0`: Reset the ABS_POS register
  - `1`: Copy the value of the ABS_POS register to the MARK register
- `speed` (float, range -15625-15625 step/s)

Description:

Move the motor at specified speed and direction. When the HOME switch turns on (the HOME switch terminal is closed), process ABS_POS register according to the ACT value.
The motor will softStop afterwards, but if the SW_MODE is set to 0 in the `/setHomeSwMode` command, it will be a hardStop instead. This command will keep the motor to the BUSY state until it stops.

The sign of the speed is the direction. A speed whose absolute value is above the range is limited to the largest register value (0xFFFFF, about 15625 step/s) by the driver library.

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `GoUntilTimeout`: Timeout while executing `/goUntil` command.
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/setGoUntilTimeout`, `/releaseSw`, `/goUntilRaw`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: An activated home switch is reported as `/error/command HomeSwActivating`, the text in the error list. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated`. It now follows `/reportError` like the other command errors.
- v2.2.0: For a motor in the servo mode, replies `/error/command InServoMode` and does nothing. Before, the command was sent to the driver. With 255, only the motors in the servo mode reply the error; the others execute the command.

#### /setGoUntilTimeout

Group: Homing. Signature: `/setGoUntilTimeout (int)motorID (int)timeOut`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `timeOut` (int, range 0-2147483647 ms, initial value 10000, configuration item `driverSettings.goUntilTimeout`): Time-out duration

Description:

Sets the time-out duration when executing `/goUntil` command. If the sensor did not detect during this time frame, the controller will regard time-out and halts the movement. Specify 0 to disable the timeout. It can also be configured from the browser configuration tool.

A negative value replies `CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. The maximum is 2147483647. The automatic hard stop at the timeout is not sent to a motor whose driver is HiZ (the timeout error is still sent).

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getGoUntilTimeout`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A negative value replies `/error/command CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. Before, it became about 49 days.
- v2.2.0: The hard stop at the timeout is not sent to a motor whose driver is HiZ, also with the brake disabled (a hard stop energizes a HiZ driver). The timeout error is still sent.

#### /getGoUntilTimeout

Group: Homing. Signature: `/getGoUntilTimeout (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns the time-out duration when executing `/goUntil` command.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/goUntilTimeout (int)motorID (int)timeout`

#### /releaseSw

Group: Homing. Signature: `/releaseSw (int)motorID (bool)ACT (bool)DIR`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `ACT` (bool)
  - `0`: Reset the ABS_POS register
  - `1`: Copy the value of the ABS_POS register to the MARK register
- `DIR` (bool)
  - `1`: Forward
  - `0`: Reverse

Description:

Move at minimum speed (5[step/s] by default) in the specified direction until the HOME switch pin becomes open. Then it will process the ABS_POS register according to the value of ACT. The process of the ACT is same as the `/goUntil` command. Then halt the motor with hardStop.

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `ReleaseSwTimeout`: Timeout while executing `/releaseSw` command.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/setReleaseSwTimeout`, `/setMinSpeed`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: `ACT` is read like the other boolean arguments (a number of 1.0 or more, or a positive integer, is true). It was read as an integer, so 0.5 was 0.
- v2.2.0: For a motor in the servo mode, replies `/error/command InServoMode` and does nothing. Before, the command was sent to the driver. With 255, only the motors in the servo mode reply the error; the others execute the command.

#### /setReleaseSwTimeout

Group: Homing. Signature: `/setReleaseSwTimeout (int)motorID (int)timeOut`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `timeOut` (int, range 0-2147483647 ms, initial value 10000, configuration item `driverSettings.releaseSwTimeout`): Time-out duration

Description:

Sets the time-out duration when executing `/releaseSw` command. If the sensor cannot be released during this time frame, halt the movement as time-out. Specify 0 to disable the timeout. It can be configured from the browser configuration tool.

A negative value replies `CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. The maximum is 2147483647. The automatic hard stop at the timeout is not sent to a motor whose driver is HiZ (the timeout error is still sent).

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getReleaseSwTimeout`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A negative value replies `/error/command CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. Before, it became about 49 days.
- v2.2.0: The hard stop at the timeout is not sent to a motor whose driver is HiZ, also with the brake disabled (a hard stop energizes a HiZ driver). The timeout error is still sent.

### HOME and LIMIT switches

#### /enableHomeSwReport

  - `0`: Disable

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):
