#### /enableSwEventReport

Group: HOME and LIMIT switches. Signature: `/enableSwEventReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value false (Disable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportSwEvn`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Sets the following message to be sent automatically when the specified motor's HOME switch terminal state drops from HIGH level to LOW (Falling Edge).
While the `/enableHomeSwReport` command observes the status by polling the STATUS register of motor driver IC from microcomputer's firmware, this `/enableSwEventReport` detects the event by driver IC's hardware, able to pick up the sensor detection shorter than 1ms.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/swEvent (int)motorID` (notification)

#### /getHomeSw

Group: HOME and LIMIT switches. Signature: `/getHomeSw (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the status of the HOME switch, closed or opened.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homeSw (int)motorID (int)swState (int)direction`

#### /enableLimitSwReport

Group: HOME and LIMIT switches. Signature: `/enableLimitSwReport (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Available on STEP400 only. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value false (Disable), configuration item `alarmAndReport.reportLimitSwStatus`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Sets automatic response when conditional change on the specified motor's LIMIT switch terminal is detected. The sent message is as same as the response from `/getLimitSw` command.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/limitSw (int)motorID (int)swState (int)direction` (notification)

#### /getLimitSw

Group: HOME and LIMIT switches. Signature: `/getLimitSw (int)motorID`. Available on STEP400 only. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns the status of LIMIT switch.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/limitSw (int)motorID (int)swState (int)direction`

#### /setHomeSwMode

Group: HOME and LIMIT switches. Signature: `/setHomeSwMode (int)motorID (bool)SW_MODE`. Executable timing: High Z state.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `SW_MODE` (bool, initial value true (User disposal (not stop)), configuration item `driverSettings.homeSwMode`): Switch mode
  - `0`: HardStop interrupt (stop immediately)
  - `1`: User disposal (not stop)

Description:

Sets switch mode whether to stop immediately when the HOME switch terminal state changes (falling edge).

The outputs must be HiZ; otherwise `MotorNotHiZ` is replied and nothing is applied.

Errors:

- `MotorNotHiZ`: The command writes a driver register that can be written only while the outputs are HiZ, and the motor is not HiZ. A motor holding its position is not HiZ: send `/softHiZ` or `/hardHiZ` first. Nothing is applied. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/getHomeSwMode`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The outputs must be HiZ (SW_MODE of the CONFIG register is writable only in HiZ); otherwise `/error/command MotorNotHiZ` and nothing is applied.

#### /getHomeSwMode

Group: HOME and LIMIT switches. Signature: `/getHomeSwMode (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Get the Switch mode described above.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homeSwMode (int)motorID (int)swMode`

See also: `/setHomeSwMode`

#### /setLimitSwMode

Group: HOME and LIMIT switches. Signature: `/setLimitSwMode (int)motorID (bool)SW_MODE`. Available on STEP400 only. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `SW_MODE` (bool, initial value true (User disposal (Does not stop)), configuration item `driverSettings.limitSwMode`): Switch mode
  - `0`: HardStop interrupt (Immediate stop)
  - `1`: User disposal (Does not stop)

Description:

Sets the Switch mode whether to stop the motor immediately when the LIMIT switch terminal condition is changed.

See also: `/getLimitSwMode`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The automatic hard stop at the limit switch (`SW_HARD_STOP`) is not sent to a motor whose driver is HiZ, also with the brake disabled (a hard stop energizes a HiZ driver).

#### /getLimitSwMode

Group: HOME and LIMIT switches. Signature: `/getLimitSwMode (int)motorID`. Available on STEP400 only. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Get the Switch mode described above.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/limitSwMode (int)motorID (int)swMode`

See also: `/setLimitSwMode`

### Position management

#### /setPosition

Group: Position management. Signature: `/setPosition (int)motorID (int)newPosition`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `newPosition` (int, range -2097152-2097151): specified coordinates

Description:

Rewrites ABS_POS register to the specified coordinates. The current motor position is set to the specified coordinates.

Do not use it while the motor is running or in the servo mode. There is no guard: if the driver refuses the write, `CommandIgnored` is sent.

A value outside the range is not rejected: the driver truncates it to 22 bits.

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getPosition`, `/resetPos`

#### /getPosition

Group: Position management. Signature: `/getPosition (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns the contents of the ABS_POS register (current position).
`/setPositionReportInterval` can make the controller to send this message with a specified interval.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/position (int)motorID (int)ABS_POS`

#### /getPositionList

Group: Position management. Signature: `/getPositionList`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments: none.

Description:

Returns the current position of all motors at once. `/getPosition 255` returns individual messages for each motor but this command returns single message with a position list.
`/setPositionListReportInterval` can make the controller to send this list with a specified interval.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/positionList (int)position1 ... (int)positionN`

See also: `/getPosition`

#### /resetPos

Group: Position management. Signature: `/resetPos (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Reset ABS_POS register to 0.

Do not use it while the motor is running or in the servo mode. There is no guard: if the driver refuses the write, `CommandIgnored` is sent.

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/setPosition`

#### /setElPos

Group: Position management. Signature: `/setElPos (int)motorID (int)newFullstep (int)newMicrostep`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `newFullstep` (int, range 0-3): Fullstep position
- `newMicrostep` (int, range 0-127): Microstep position

Description:

Set the electrical position of the motor. The microstep is expressed in step/128, and the value has to be matched with the current microstep mode.

Use it while the motor is HiZ. There is no guard on the motor state: the L6470 also refuses the write while the motor is stopped and energized (which the datasheet allows), and then `CommandIgnored` is sent.

A full step outside 0-3 or a microstep outside 0-127 replies `CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied.

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getElPos`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A full step outside 0-3 or a microstep outside 0-127 replies `/error/command CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. Before, they were clamped.

#### /getElPos

Group: Position management. Signature: `/getElPos (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns the current electrical position of the motor.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/elPos (int)motorID (int)fullstep (int)microstep`

#### /setMark

Group: Position management. Signature: `/setMark (int)motorID (int)MARK`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `MARK` (int): Coordination to be set

Description:

Set the MARK register to arbitrary position.

A value outside the range is not rejected: the driver truncates it to 22 bits.

See also: `/getMark`, `/goMark`

#### /getMark

Group: Position management. Signature: `/getMark (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Get the MARK position.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/mark (int)motorID (int)MARK`

#### /goHome

Group: Position management. Signature: `/goHome (int)motorID`. Executable timing: In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Move the motor to the HOME position (zero position) according to the speed profile.

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Judges its direction correctly when the home switch or the limit switch prohibits a motion (`/setProhibitMotionOnHomeSw`, `/setProhibitMotionOnLimitSw`): it is the sign of the 22-bit difference to the target, the way the driver goes (the shortest way). The direction was reversed for a target less than 2048 steps away (so a short move away from the switch was refused with `HomeSwActivating` / `LimitSwActivating` and a short move towards it was started), and wrong again beyond 2^21 steps.
- v2.2.0: On a busy motor, the STATUS register is read with GetParam, which does not clear the latched flags. Before, it was read with GetStatus, so the status poll could miss a flag and the report (`/overCurrent`, `/stall`, `/swEvent`, `/uvlo`, ...) was lost.

#### /goMark

Group: Position management. Signature: `/goMark (int)motorID`. Executable timing: In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Move the motor to the MARK position according to the speed profile.

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/setMark`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Judges its direction correctly when the home switch or the limit switch prohibits a motion (`/setProhibitMotionOnHomeSw`, `/setProhibitMotionOnLimitSw`): it is the sign of the 22-bit difference to the target, the way the driver goes (the shortest way). The direction was reversed for a target less than 2048 steps away (so a short move away from the switch was refused with `HomeSwActivating` / `LimitSwActivating` and a short move towards it was started), and wrong again beyond 2^21 steps.
- v2.2.0: On a busy motor, the STATUS register is read with GetParam, which does not clear the latched flags. Before, it was read with GetStatus, so the status poll could miss a flag and the report (`/overCurrent`, `/stall`, `/swEvent`, `/uvlo`, ...) was lost.

### Motor control

#### /run

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/run (int)motorID (float)speed`. Executable timing: In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `speed` (float, range -15625-15625 step/s): Rotation speed

Description:

Rotates the motor at specified speed. The acceleration is controlled with the pre-set speed profile. The speed is limited by maxSpeed. It remains in the BUSY state until the motor reaches the specified speed.

The sign of the speed is the direction. A speed whose absolute value is above the range is limited to the largest register value (0xFFFFF, about 15625 step/s) by the driver library.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/runRaw`, `/combine/run`

#### /move

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/move (int)motorID (int)step`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped, In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `step` (int): Moving step counts

Description:

Moves specified number of steps according to the pre-set speed profile. It remains in the BUSY state until it reaches the specified step count. This command can only execute when the motor is stopped.

A step count whose absolute value is above 4,194,303 (22 bits) is not rejected: it is limited to 4,194,303 by the driver library.

While the motor is turning, the driver ignores the command and the board replies `CommandIgnored` (not `MotorNotStopped`).

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.
- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/combine/move`

#### /goTo

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/goTo (int)motorID (int)position`. Executable timing: In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `position` (int, range -2097152-2097151): Destination

Description:

Moves to the specified position in the shortest route according to the pre-set speed profile. Remains in the BUSY state until it finishes moving to the specified position.
Inside the driver, -2,097,152 and 2,097,151 are located next to each other in a loop.

A position outside the range is not rejected. A position above 4,194,303 is limited to 4,194,303 by the driver library, which the driver reads as -1. Any other position is cut to its lower 22 bits and read as a signed number: 2,097,152 becomes -2,097,152 and -2,097,153 becomes 2,097,151.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/goToDir`, `/combine/goTo`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Judges its direction correctly when the home switch or the limit switch prohibits a motion (`/setProhibitMotionOnHomeSw`, `/setProhibitMotionOnLimitSw`): it is the sign of the 22-bit difference to the target, the way the driver goes (the shortest way). The direction was reversed for a target less than 2048 steps away (so a short move away from the switch was refused with `HomeSwActivating` / `LimitSwActivating` and a short move towards it was started), and wrong again beyond 2^21 steps.
- v2.2.0: On a busy motor, the STATUS register is read with GetParam, which does not clear the latched flags. Before, it was read with GetStatus, so the status poll could miss a flag and the report (`/overCurrent`, `/stall`, `/swEvent`, `/uvlo`, ...) was lost.

#### /goToDir

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/goToDir (int)motorID (bool)DIR (int)position`. Executable timing: In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `DIR` (bool): Rotation direction
- `position` (int, range -2097152-2097151): Destination

Description:

Moves to the specified position in the specified direction according to the pre-set speed profile. Remains in the BUSY state until it finishes moving to the specified position.

A position outside the range is not rejected. A position above 4,194,303 is limited to 4,194,303 by the driver library, which the driver reads as -1. Any other position is cut to its lower 22 bits and read as a signed number: 2,097,152 becomes -2,097,152 and -2,097,153 becomes 2,097,151.

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/goTo`, `/combine/goToDir`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: On a busy motor, the STATUS register is read with GetParam, which does not clear the latched flags. Before, it was read with GetStatus, so the status poll could miss a flag and the report (`/overCurrent`, `/stall`, `/swEvent`, `/uvlo`, ...) was lost.

#### /softStop

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/softStop (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

After decelerating according to the speed profile, the motor stops while it is kept excited. Remains in the BUSY state until the motor stops. If it was originally in the High Z state, the motor will be excited while it keeps its position.
If it was in the servo mode, the mode will be released.

With the electromagnetic brake enabled, the command does nothing while the brake is engaged or after `/free` (the motor is HiZ). During the deceleration of `/softHiZ` or `/activate 0` (brake state 3), the command is executed and cancels the engaging: the brake stays released (state 2).

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

See also: `/combine/softStop`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: With the brake enabled, does nothing while the brake is engaged or after `/free` (motor HiZ). Before, it energized the motor and left the brake state engaged, so `/activate 0` and `/hardHiZ` could not make the motor HiZ again.
- v2.2.0: Cancels pending motion, also for a motor with the brake disabled: a `/goTo`, `/goToDir`, `/goHome` or `/goMark` waiting for the BUSY flag to clear (it was sent when the motor became not busy, so a stopped motor started again), the homing (its timeout sent a hard stop, which energized a motor made HiZ in the meantime) and the servo mode.

#### /hardStop

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/hardStop (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Immediately stops the motor and leaves it excited. Remains in the BUSY state until the motor stops. If it was originally in the High Z state, the motor is excited while it keeps its position.
If it was in the servo mode, the mode will be released.

With the electromagnetic brake enabled, the command does nothing while the brake is engaged or after `/free` (the motor is HiZ). During the deceleration of `/softHiZ` or `/activate 0` (brake state 3), the command is executed and cancels the engaging: the brake stays released (state 2).

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

See also: `/combine/hardStop`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: With the brake enabled, does nothing while the brake is engaged or after `/free` (motor HiZ). Before, it energized the motor and left the brake state engaged, so `/activate 0` and `/hardHiZ` could not make the motor HiZ again.
- v2.2.0: Cancels pending motion, also for a motor with the brake disabled: a `/goTo`, `/goToDir`, `/goHome` or `/goMark` waiting for the BUSY flag to clear (it was sent when the motor became not busy, so a stopped motor started again), the homing (its timeout sent a hard stop, which energized a motor made HiZ in the meantime) and the servo mode.

#### /softHiZ

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/softHiZ (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Decelerate according to the speed profile, then stop the motor and release excitation. When the excitation is released, it goes into the High Z state. It remains in the BUSY state until the motor is stopped.
If it was in the servo mode, it will be released.
if the electromagnetic brake is enabled, the controller puts the brake into hold state, and then transits to High Z state.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

See also: `/combine/softHiZ`, `/enableElectromagnetBrake`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: With the brake enabled, on a stopped motor the brake is engaged at the next status read (up to 5 ms later). The stop is judged on a status read after the command.
- v2.2.0: A motion command (`/run`, `/move`, `/goTo`, ...) or `/activate 1` during the deceleration cancels the engaging; the brake stays released. Before, the brake engaged when the motor stopped later.
- v2.2.0: After `/free`, the brake is engaged at once (the motor is already HiZ).
- v2.2.0: Cancels pending motion, also for a motor with the brake disabled: a `/goTo`, `/goToDir`, `/goHome` or `/goMark` waiting for the BUSY flag to clear (it was sent when the motor became not busy, so a stopped motor started again), the homing (its timeout sent a hard stop, which energized a motor made HiZ in the meantime) and the servo mode.

#### /hardHiZ

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/hardHiZ (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Immediately stops the motor and releases the stepper excitation. When the motor excitation is released, it goes into the High Z state. Remains in the BUSY state until the motor is stopped.
If it was in the servo mode, it will be released.
if the electromagnetic brake is enabled, the controller puts the brake into hold state, and then transits to High Z state.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

See also: `/combine/hardHiZ`, `/enableElectromagnetBrake`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A single motor no longer sends a soft stop before the hard HiZ; a single motor, all motors (255) and `/combine/hardHiZ` behave the same. With the brake enabled and released (after `/activate 1`), the motor is stopped with a hard stop (still energized) before the brake is engaged, so it does not keep running during the brake transition time. While the brake is engaged or engaging, the command does nothing as before.
- v2.2.0: After `/free`, the brake is engaged at once (the motor is already HiZ).
- v2.2.0: Cancels pending motion, also for a motor with the brake disabled: a `/goTo`, `/goToDir`, `/goHome` or `/goMark` waiting for the BUSY flag to clear (it was sent when the motor became not busy, so a stopped motor started again), the homing (its timeout sent a hard stop, which energized a motor made HiZ in the meantime) and the servo mode.

#### /combine/run

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/combine/run (int)motorID1 (int)motorID2 (float)speed`. Executable timing: In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID1` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `motorID2` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `speed` (float, range -15625-15625 step/s): Rotation speed

Description:

Same as `/run` for two motors. The sign of the speed is the direction. A speed whose absolute value is above the range is limited to the largest register value (0xFFFFF, about 15625 step/s) by the driver library.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/run`

#### /combine/move

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/combine/move (int)motorID1 (int)motorID2 (int)step`. Executable timing: When the motor is stopped, In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID1` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `motorID2` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `step` (int): Moving step counts

Description:

Same as `/move` for two motors. A step count whose absolute value is above 4,194,303 (22 bits) is not rejected: it is limited to 4,194,303 by the driver library.

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/move`

#### /combine/goTo

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/combine/goTo (int)motorID1 (int)motorID2 (int)position`. Executable timing: In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID1` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `motorID2` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `position` (int, range -2097152-2097151): Destination

Description:

Same as `/goTo` for two motors. A position outside the range is not rejected. A position above 4,194,303 is limited to 4,194,303 by the driver library, which the driver reads as -1. Any other position is cut to its lower 22 bits and read as a signed number: 2,097,152 becomes -2,097,152 and -2,097,153 becomes 2,097,151.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/goTo`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Judges its direction correctly when the home switch or the limit switch prohibits a motion (`/setProhibitMotionOnHomeSw`, `/setProhibitMotionOnLimitSw`): it is the sign of the 22-bit difference to the target, the way the driver goes (the shortest way). The direction was reversed for a target less than 2048 steps away (so a short move away from the switch was refused with `HomeSwActivating` / `LimitSwActivating` and a short move towards it was started), and wrong again beyond 2^21 steps.

#### /combine/goToDir

Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. #### /combine/softStop

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/combine/softStop (int)motorID1 (int)motorID2`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID1` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `motorID2` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

#### /runRaw

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/runRaw (int)motorID (int)speed`. Executable timing: In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `speed` (int): Rotation speed (raw register value, signed)

Description:

Rotates the motor at the specified speed using a raw register value. The sign of the speed value determines the direction.

A speed outside the 20-bit range is limited to 20 bits by the driver.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/run`, `/combine/runRaw`

#### /goUntilRaw

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/goUntilRaw (int)motorID (bool)ACT (int)speed`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `ACT` (bool): Same as `/goUntil`
- `speed` (int): Speed (raw register value, signed)

Description:

Same as `/goUntil` but uses a raw register value for speed. The sign of the speed value determines the direction.

The speed is limited to 20 bits (0xFFFFF) by the firmware and the driver libraries. `/goUntilRaw 255` (all motors) interprets the speed as a raw register value, like for a single motor.

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).
- `GoUntilTimeout`: Timeout while executing `/goUntil` command.
- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `InServoMode`: Received a command which can not be executed while servo mode. **v2.2.0**: Also sent for `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw` and `/releaseSw`.

See also: `/goUntil`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Limits the speed to 20 bits (`0xFFFFF`), like `/runRaw`. Larger values were sent as is, and the driver ignored the upper bits.
- v2.2.0: `/goUntilRaw 255` (all motors) interprets the speed as a raw register value, like for a single motor. It was treated as steps/s.
- v2.2.0: An activated home switch is reported as `/error/command HomeSwActivating`, the text in the error list. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated`. It now follows `/reportError` like the other command errors.
- v2.2.0: For a motor in the servo mode, replies `/error/command InServoMode` and does nothing. Before, the command was sent to the driver. With 255, only the motors in the servo mode reply the error; the others execute the command.

#### /combine/runRaw

Group: Motor control. Signature: `/combine/runRaw (int)motorID1 (int)motorID2 (int)speed`. Executable timing: In motion start condition.

Arguments:

- `motorID2` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `speed` (int): Rotation speed (raw register value, signed)

A speed outside the 20-bit range is limited to 20 bits by the driver.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `HomeSwActivating`: Movement from home switch position towards the origin point. Also sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. **v2.2.0**: Sent by `/goUntil` and `/goUntilRaw` when the home switch is already activated. It was sent as `HomeSwActivated` before.
- `LimitSwActivating`: Movement from limit switch position towards the opposite direction from origin.

### Electromagnetic brake

#### /enableElectromagnetBrake

Group: Electromagnetic brake. Signature: `/enableElectromagnetBrake (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool, initial value false (Disable), configuration item `driverSettings.electromagnetBrakeEnable`)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Enables / disables the electromagnetic brake.
While the brake is enabled, the controller replies the `BrakeEngaged` (`/error/command`) if motor movement command is sent without releasing the electromagnetic brake.

The setting is changed only while the driver is HiZ, and the brake is disabled only while it is engaged or after `/free`; otherwise the command replies `CommandIgnored`. Sending the current value does nothing. After a change, the brake output is engaged and the brake state is engaged. The same rule applies to a configuration loaded over USB serial (a warning is printed for a motor that is not changed).

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/activate`, `/free`, `/setBrakeTransitionDuration`, `/getBrakeStatus`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Changes the setting only while the driver is HiZ, and disables the brake only while it is engaged or after `/free`; otherwise `/error/command CommandIgnored`. Sending the current value does nothing. After a change the brake output is engaged and the state is engaged. Before, disabling a released brake engaged it on a turning motor, and enabling it on an energized motor left a state where `/activate 0` and `/hardHiZ` did nothing.

#### /activate

Group: Electromagnetic brake. Signature: `/activate (int)motorID (bool)state`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `state` (bool)
  - `1`: Motor excited, EM brake released
  - `0`: Motor not excited, EM brake engaged

Description:

Switches motor excitation / release when the electromagnetic brake is enabled. The electromagnetic brake (EM) also works conjunction with the motor. You cannot send motor movement command when the motor is not excited by this command.
If the electromagnetic brake is disabled, this command is ignored: only `CommandIgnored` is sent, and pending motion is not cancelled.

`/activate 1` while the brake is released does nothing. From the engaged state it energizes the driver and releases the brake after `brakeTransitionDuration`, but only if a status read after the command shows the driver energized (during the engaging it goes back to the release sequence (the transition time starts again), during the stopping it only cancels the engaging, after `/free` it releases at once). If the driver stays HiZ (for example without motor power), the brake stays engaged and `BrakeReleaseFailed` is sent.

`/activate 0` on a turning motor decelerates it and engages the brake when it has stopped, like `/softHiZ`; on a stopped motor the brake is engaged at the next status read (up to 5 ms later). The driver goes HiZ after `brakeTransitionDuration`. The brake state can be read with `/getBrakeStatus`.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).
- `BrakeReleaseFailed`: `/activate 1` was sent but the driver stayed HiZ (for example without motor power), so the brake stays engaged. Added in v2.2.0.

See also: `/enableElectromagnetBrake`, `/free`, `/getBrakeStatus`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: `/activate 1` while the brake is released does nothing. Before, it sent a hard stop, which stopped a turning motor abruptly.
- v2.2.0: `/activate 1` releases the brake only if a status read after the command shows the driver energized. If the driver stays HiZ (e.g. no motor power), the brake stays engaged and `/error/command BrakeReleaseFailed motorID` is sent. Before, the brake was released after `brakeTransitionDuration` in any case.
- v2.2.0: `/activate 1` during the deceleration of `/softHiZ` (or `/activate 0`) cancels the engaging and keeps the brake released; the deceleration goes on. Before, it stopped the motor with a hard stop, and the brake still engaged when the motor stopped.
- v2.2.0: `/activate 0` on a turning motor decelerates it and engages the brake when it has stopped, like `/softHiZ`. Before, it engaged the brake without stopping the motor.
- v2.2.0: `/activate 0` on a stopped motor engages the brake at the next status read (up to 5 ms later). The stop is now judged on a status read after the command.
- v2.2.0: After `/free`: `/activate 1` returns the motor to the released (energized) state, and `/activate 0` engages the brake at once (the motor is already HiZ).
- v2.2.0: KVAL_HOLD (TVAL_HOLD in the current mode) is raised to at least half of KVAL_RUN (TVAL_RUN) whenever the motor is energized again: from engaged or engaging (as before), and now also after `/free`.
- v2.2.0: `/activate 0` cancels pending motion of a motor with the brake enabled (with the brake disabled it replies `CommandIgnored` and cancels nothing): a `/goTo`, `/goToDir`, `/goHome` or `/goMark` waiting for the BUSY flag to clear (it was sent when the motor became not busy, so a stopped motor started again), the homing (its timeout sent a hard stop, which energized a motor made HiZ in the meantime) and the servo mode.

#### /free

Group: Electromagnetic brake. Signature: `/free (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Releases motor axis when the electromagnetic brake is enabled. It releases motor excitation and keep EM brake in release state.
Be cautious when sending this command. If some load is hanged to the motor, it will loose the hold and the load may fall down.
If the electromagnetic brake is disabled, this command is ignored: only `CommandIgnored` is sent, and pending motion is not cancelled.

After `/free`, a stop of the motor no longer engages the brake (when `/free` was sent during the deceleration of `/softHiZ`). A motion command (`/run`, `/move`, `/goTo`, ...) or `/activate 1` energizes the motor again and returns it to the released state. `/activate 0`, `/softHiZ` and `/hardHiZ` engage the brake at once.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/enableElectromagnetBrake`, `/activate`, `/getBrakeStatus`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: After `/free`, a stop of the motor no longer engages the brake (when `/free` was sent during the deceleration of `/softHiZ`).
- v2.2.0: After `/free`, a motion command (`/run`, `/move`, `/goTo`, ...) is executed and the motor returns to the released (energized) state. `/activate 1` does the same. `/activate 0`, `/softHiZ` and `/hardHiZ` engage the brake at once (the motor is already HiZ).
- v2.2.0: KVAL_HOLD (TVAL_HOLD in the current mode) is raised to at least half of KVAL_RUN (TVAL_RUN) when the motor is energized again after `/free`. Before, the motor was energized with the configured holding value.
- v2.2.0: `/free` cancels pending motion of a motor with the brake enabled (with the brake disabled it replies `CommandIgnored`): a `/goTo`, `/goToDir`, `/goHome` or `/goMark` waiting for the BUSY flag to clear (it was sent when the motor became not busy, so a stopped motor started again), the homing (its timeout sent a hard stop, which energized a motor made HiZ in the meantime) and the servo mode.

#### /setBrakeTransitionDuration

Group: Electromagnetic brake. Signature: `/setBrakeTransitionDuration (int)motorID (int)duration`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `duration` (int, range 0-65535 ms, initial value 100, configuration item `driverSettings.brakeTransitionDuration`): Transition duration

Description:

Sets the transitional duration to keep the motor excited when the electromagnetic brake is activated or released. This is to keep holding the motor axis until the brake movement is completed, due to the physical transition time for the brake mechanism.

A value outside 0-65535 replies `CommandIgnored` and the setting is kept. The release after `/activate` comes 0-5 ms after the set time, because the brake is handled every 5 ms.

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getBrakeTransitionDuration`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A value outside 0-65535 replies `/error/command CommandIgnored` and keeps the setting. Before, the value was taken as a 16-bit unsigned integer, so only its lower 16 bits were used (65536 became 0, -1 became 65535).
- v2.2.0: The brake times are in 5 ms steps: the release after `/activate 1` comes 0-5 ms after `brakeTransitionDuration` (measured 99.8-105.4 ms for 100 ms; before 99.8-107.6 ms), and the engage after a stop or a HiZ is judged at the next status read.

#### /getBrakeTransitionDuration

Group: Electromagnetic brake. Signature: `/getBrakeTransitionDuration (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns the transitional duration to keep holding the motor axis when the electromagnetic brake is activated or released.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/brakeTransitionDuration (int)motorID (int)duration`

#### /getBrakeStatus

Group: Electromagnetic brake. Signature: `/getBrakeStatus (int)motorID`. Added in v2.2.0. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Returns the state of the electromagnetic brake of the specified motor. The state is -1 for a motor with the brake disabled.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/brakeStatus (int)motorID (int)state`

See also: `/activate`, `/free`, `/enableElectromagnetBrake`

### Servo mode

#### /enableServoMode

Group: Servo mode. Signature: `/enableServoMode (int)motorID (bool)enable`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `enable` (bool)
  - `1`: Enable
  - `0`: Disable

Description:

Turns on/off the servo mode (position tracking mode). To avoid sudden movement, the current position at the moment of activation is set to the target position.
It is not possible to send other motor control commands such as `/run` or `/goTo` while operating in this mode.

Enabling the servo mode turns off the BUSY, motor status and direction reports (`/enableBusyReport`, `/enableMotorStatusReport`, `/enableDirReport`) of the motor. Disabling the servo mode does not turn them on again; send the enable commands again if needed. It also resets the integral term and the previous error of the PID controller. While in the servo mode, `/goUntil`, `/goUntilRaw`, `/releaseSw` and `/homing` reply `InServoMode`.

With the electromagnetic brake enabled, `/enableServoMode 1` replies `BrakeEngaged` and does nothing while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (while stopping or after `/free` the command is executed); `/enableServoMode 0` does nothing while the brake is engaged or after `/free`.

When the driver goes HiZ by itself (overcurrent shutdown, thermal shutdown, UVLO) in the servo mode, the servo mode is cancelled and `ServoModeCancelledOnHiZ` is sent (`BrakeEngagedOnHiZ` too, with the brake enabled). Enable the servo mode again with `/enableServoMode 1`; the current position becomes the target.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/homingStatus (int)motorID (int)homingStatus` (when: While homing is in progress)

Errors:

- `BrakeEngaged`: A motion command was sent while the electromagnetic brake was active. Also sent for `/enableServoMode 1` and `/homing` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`).

See also: `/setTargetPosition`, `/setServoParam`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: With the brake enabled, `/enableServoMode 1` while the brake is engaged, releasing or engaging (not while stopping or after `/free`) replies `/error/command BrakeEngaged` and does nothing. Before, it energized and moved the motor with the brake engaged.
- v2.2.0: With the brake enabled, `/enableServoMode 0` while the brake is engaged or after `/free` (motor HiZ) does nothing. Before, it energized the motor.
- v2.2.0: When a driver goes HiZ by itself (overcurrent shutdown, thermal shutdown, UVLO) in the servo mode, the servo mode is cancelled and `/error/command ServoModeCancelledOnHiZ` is sent (follows `/reportError`), with or without the brake. With the brake enabled, `BrakeEngagedOnHiZ` is also sent. Before, with the brake disabled the next servo update energized the driver again. The commands that make the driver HiZ cancel the servo mode first and do not send this error.
- v2.2.0: Enabling the servo mode resets the integral and the previous error of the PID controller. The previous values were kept from the last time the servo mode was used.
- v2.2.0: The update period is 5 ms instead of 10 ms (and no longer varies between 7 and 13 ms when position reports are enabled; an OSC message that sends several replies can still delay one update, up to 7.75 ms measured). The integral and derivative terms are scaled by the period, so the same `kP`, `kI` and `kD` were designed to give about the same response; retune the gains if needed.
- v2.2.0: STEP400: the home switch and the limit switch are judged separately. A pressed home switch stops the motion towards `homingDirection` (with `/setProhibitMotionOnHomeSw` or the home switch in the hard stop mode), and a pressed limit switch stops the motion away from `homingDirection` (with `/setProhibitMotionOnLimitSw` or the limit switch in the hard stop mode), as before. While the home switch was pressed, the limit switch was not checked. Only a motor with both switches pressed behaves differently.
- v2.2.0: The automatic hard stop at a switch event in the servo mode is not sent to a motor whose driver is HiZ.
- v2.2.0: Cancels pending motion, also for a motor with the brake disabled: a `/goTo`, `/goToDir`, `/goHome` or `/goMark` waiting for the BUSY flag to clear (it was sent when the motor became not busy, so a stopped motor started again), the homing (its timeout sent a hard stop, which energized a motor made HiZ in the meantime) and the servo mode.

#### /setServoParam

Group: Servo mode. Signature: `/setServoParam (int)motorID (float)kP (float)kI (float)kD`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `kP` (float, initial value 0.06, configuration item `servoMode.kP`): Proportional control gain
- `kI` (float, initial value 0, configuration item `servoMode.kI`): Integral control gain
- `kD` (float, initial value 0, configuration item `servoMode.kD`): Differential control gain

Description:

Adjusts the PID control gain.

A negative gain replies `CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. The update period of the servo mode is 5 ms; the integral and derivative terms are scaled by the period.

Errors:

- `CommandIgnored`: The command is currently not executable. Also refer Timing section. Also sent when a value is outside the range of the command; nothing is applied (the motor ID is 255 for `/setPositionListReportInterval`).

See also: `/getServoParam`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A negative gain replies `/error/command CommandIgnored` and nothing is applied. Before, it was set to 0.
- v2.2.0: The servo update period is 5 ms instead of 10 ms. The same gains were designed to give about the same response, but retune them if needed.

#### /getServoParam

Group: Servo mode. Signature: `/getServoParam (int)motorID`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID

Description:

Gets the PID gains (kP, kI, kD) of the servo mode.

Replies and notifications (see Messages from the board):

- `/servoParam (int)motorID (float)kP (float)kI (float)kD`

#### /setTargetPosition

Group: Servo mode. Signature: `/setTargetPosition (int)motorID (int)position`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800), 255 (all motors)): Motor ID
- `position` (int, range -2097152-2097151): target position

Description:

Sets the target position in servo mode.

See also: `/enableServoMode`, `/setTargetPositionList`

#### /setTargetPositionList

Group: Servo mode. Signature: `/setTargetPositionList (int)position1 ... (int)positionN`. Executable timing: Always.

Arguments:

- `position1 ... positionN` (int, range -2097152-2097151): target position

Description:

Sets the target positions of the servo mode for all axes at once.

See also: `/setTargetPosition`

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A message with fewer positions than the number of motors replies `/error/osc MissingArgument` and nothing is applied. Before, the missing positions became 0 and a servo-mode motor ran to 0.

## Messages from the board

#### /destIp

Signature: `/destIp (int)destIp[0] (int)destIp[1] (int)destIp[2] (int)destIp[3] (int)isNewDestIp`.

Arguments:

- `destIp[0]` (int, range 0-255): Each byte of destIp
- `destIp[1]` (int, range 0-255): Each byte of destIp
- `destIp[2]` (int, range 0-255): Each byte of destIp
- `destIp[3]` (int, range 0-255): Each byte of destIp
- `isNewDestIp` (int, range 0-1): Indicates if destIp has been changed. 1 if it has been changed, or 0 if the same address has already been set.

Changes:

- v2.2.0: When the `/setDestIp` starts the resolution of the MAC address (the first one, one from another address, or one 1.5 s or more after the last packet from the destination), the message is sent once it has been resolved, so it can come a few seconds later (it depends on the route, such as Wi-Fi); otherwise it is sent at once. If it does not come, send `/setDestIp` again.

#### /version

Signature: `/version (string)version`.

Arguments:

- `version` (string)

#### /configName

Signature: `/configName (string)configName (int)sdInitializeSucceeded (int)configFileOpenSucceeded (int)configFileParseSucceeded (string)configFilename`.

Arguments:

- `configName` (string): The configuration name (`information.configName` of the configuration file that was read). It is `Default` when no file was read or the file has no name. `/setConfigName` changes it.
- `sdInitializeSucceeded` (int, range 0-1): 1 if the microSD card could be used at start-up. 0 if there was no card, the card is not FAT16 or FAT32 (for example exFAT). The card is checked only at start-up.
- `configFileOpenSucceeded` (int, range 0-1): 1 if `config.txt` could be opened or a valid `.json` file was read. 0 if neither (including a first `.json` file that is invalid). See the table below.
- `configFileParseSucceeded` (int, range 0-1): 1 if a configuration file was read and its values were applied (a `config.txt` that could be parsed as JSON, or a valid `.json` file, which has `information.configVersion`). 0 if the defaults are used.
- `configFilename` (string): The path of the configuration file that was read, with a leading `/` (e.g., `/config.txt` or `/STEP400_venue-A.json`). When no file was read, it is `/config.txt`, where `/saveConfig` saves. `F<path>` over USB serial changes it. The path is at most 63 characters. This is the on-disk path, distinct from `configName` which is the user-editable label. Added in v2.1.0.

Changes:

- v2.2.0: A file whose name starts with `.` (for example `._name.json`, which macOS writes next to each file it copies to the card) is no longer a candidate for the configuration file. Before, such a file could come first among the `.json` files and, being invalid, hid every valid `.json` file after it.
- v2.2.0: The values of a configuration file that was not accepted are no longer applied: a first `.json` file that cannot be parsed or has no `information.configVersion` (it ends the search), and a `config.txt` that failed to parse in the middle. Now the defaults are used, as with no card. Before, the values of such a file were still used, even when it was reported as not loaded (`configName` showed its name).

#### /saveConfig

Signature: `/saveConfig (string)message`. Added in v2.1.0.

Arguments:

- `message` (string): `Saved to SD. Reboot to apply.`

#### /error/saveConfig

Signature: `/error/saveConfig (string)errorText`. Added in v2.1.0.

Arguments:

- `errorText` (string)
  - `SD open failed`: The card was usable at start-up, but the file could not be written: the card was removed after start-up, the card or the folder is full, the folder does not exist, or a write error. If the temporary file could not be written, the saved file stays as it was.
  - `No SD card`: There was no usable card at start-up: no card, or a card that is not FAT16 or FAT32 (for example exFAT). A card inserted after start-up is not used until the board restarts.

#### /microstepMode

Signature: `/microstepMode (int)motorID (int)STEP_SEL`.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800)): Motor ID
- `STEP_SEL` (int, range 0-7): Microstepping mode
  - `0`: Full-step
  - `1`: Half-step
  - `2`: 1/4 microstep
  - `3`: 1/8 microstep
  - `4`: 1/16 microstep
  - `5`: 1/32 microstep
  - `6`: 1/64 microstep
  - `7`: 1/128 microstep

- `lowSpeedOptimizeThreshold` (float, range 0-976.3 step/s): Low speed optimization threshold
- `optimizationEnabled` (int)
  - `1`: Low speed optimization enabled
  - `0`: Low speed optimization disabled

Changes:

- v2.2.0: The third argument `optimizationEnabled` is sent with the integer type tag `i` (0 / 1). Before, it used `T` / `F`. Clients that expect `T` / `F` must be updated.

#### /overCurrent

Signature: `/overCurrent (int)motorID`.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800)): Motor ID

Description:

Sent at once when the overcurrent condition starts (if no such report of the motor went out in the last 200 ms) and then, while it lasts, at most every 200 ms per motor. Detections within the 200 ms are not lost: they give one message at the end of the interval. Detections while the report is disabled (`/enableOverCurrentReport`) are not sent later.

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Sent at once when the condition starts (if no such report of the motor went out in the last 200 ms) and then, while it lasts, at most every 200 ms per motor. Before, it was sent at every status read while the condition lasted (every 10 ms). The message is unchanged.

#### /overCurrentThreshold

Signature: `/overCurrentThreshold (int)motorID (float)overCurrentThreshold`.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800)): Motor ID
- `overCurrentThreshold` (float, range 312.5-10000 (STEP400), 375-6000 (STEP800) mA): thresholds in [mA].

#### /stall

Signature: `/stall (int)motorID`.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800)): Motor ID

Description:

Sent at once when the stall condition starts (if no such report of the motor went out in the last 200 ms) and then, while it lasts, at most every 200 ms per motor. Detections within the 200 ms are not lost: they give one message at the end of the interval. Detections while the report is disabled (`/enableStallReport`) are not sent later.

Stall detection lets the driver detect, from the motor current, that the motor can no longer turn against the load. Find a threshold (`/setStallThreshold`) as close as possible to, and slightly above, the current actually flowing. A small loss of steps cannot be detected, but a large position error may be.

Changes:

- v2.2.0: Sent at once when the condition starts (if no such report of the motor went out in the last 200 ms) and then, while it lasts, at most every 200 ms per motor. Before, it was sent at every status read while the condition lasted (every 10 ms). The message is unchanged.

#### /stallThreshold

Signature: `/stallThreshold (int)motorID (float)stallThreshold`.

Arguments:

- `motorID` (int, range 1-4 (STEP400), 1-8 (STEP800)): Motor ID
- `stallThreshold` (float, range 312.5-10000 (STEP400), 31.25-4000 (STEP800) mA): thresholds in [mA]
